requirements.requirement: Primary persona is 최재원, a second-year student in Seoul National University Electrical and Computer Engineering.
requirements.acceptance: Demo profile and product documentation reflect the persona; school/major storage remains optional and private.

requirements.requirement: Default locale is Korean, currency is KRW, and timezone is Asia/Seoul.
requirements.acceptance: Dates, money, week boundaries, reminders, and seed data use ko-KR, KRW, and Asia/Seoul.

requirements.requirement: The user lives in a two-room rental with one friend and needs shared-home operations.
requirements.acceptance: A household can contain the user and one roommate, while the schema remains extensible to more members.

requirements.requirement: Demo household inventory reflects chicken breast as a fixed lunch item and Monster drinks split between refrigerated and room-temperature storage.
requirements.acceptance: Demo data includes chicken breast and Monster items in appropriate locations without treating all Monster cans as refrigerated.

requirements.requirement: The product is a student personal operating system, not an enterprise finance product.
requirements.acceptance: UI language, density, onboarding, and feature scope remain simple and student-friendly.

requirements.requirement: The product must be mobile-first but fully usable on desktop as a responsive PWA.
requirements.acceptance: Core journeys pass at 360px mobile width and desktop widths; installable PWA behavior is present where supported.

requirements.requirement: Primary navigation contains Home, Tutoring, Money, Household, and Settings.
requirements.acceptance: All five top-level destinations exist and are reachable from persistent mobile/desktop navigation.

requirements.requirement: A global quick-add action supports lesson, income, expense, payment/deposit handling, inventory, and shared expense creation.
requirements.acceptance: Quick-add is reachable in one tap/click and opens context-aware creation actions.

requirements.requirement: The app unifies tutoring work, cash movement, subscriptions, surplus allocation, and household operations without duplicating records.
requirements.acceptance: Cross-module links use a single source record plus references rather than copied amounts.

requirements.requirement: Financial data distinguishes work performed, money receivable, planned obligation, and actual account movement.
requirements.acceptance: Lesson, receivable, subscription occurrence/shared expense, and financial transaction are separate entities.

requirements.requirement: Money analytics include monthly cash flow, spending by category, tutoring income by student, effective hourly income, fixed/subscription costs, and asset trend.
requirements.acceptance: Analytics page renders each metric from real domain queries with empty/loading/error states.

requirements.requirement: Settings include profile, categories, accounts, tutoring defaults, integrations, notifications, and data export/backup.
requirements.acceptance: Each settings area has a functional page or explicitly labeled deferred adapter without dead controls.

requirements.requirement: All user-visible monetary values use integer KRW semantics and never floating-point arithmetic.
requirements.acceptance: Database uses bigint or numeric integer amounts; TypeScript domain converters prevent precision loss.

requirements.requirement: All derived totals must have a single documented formula and automated tests.
requirements.acceptance: Formula module and unit tests cover dashboard, settlement, subscription normalization, and surplus totals.

requirements.requirement: The app must have clear loading, empty, offline, stale-sync, and recoverable error states.
requirements.acceptance: Every data surface provides accessible status feedback and safe retry behavior.

requirements.requirement: No production deployment, production database mutation, financial transfer, or investment trade occurs automatically.
requirements.acceptance: External writes require explicit user action and production changes require explicit operator confirmation.

requirements.requirement: Students have tutoring type SUBJECT or SCHOOL_RECORD (생기부).
requirements.acceptance: Student form requires exactly one tutoring type and filters relevant fields.

requirements.requirement: SUBJECT tutoring permits only Mathematics, Physics, or Chemistry.
requirements.acceptance: UI, validation, database constraint, and tests reject every other subject.

requirements.requirement: SCHOOL_RECORD tutoring has no academic subject value.
requirements.acceptance: Subject is null and hidden for SCHOOL_RECORD; database check constraint enforces this.

requirements.requirement: Each student has a default lesson mode of online video or in-person.
requirements.acceptance: Student creation requires a default mode and conditionally requires location or Meet behavior.

requirements.requirement: Each lesson copies the student's default mode but can override it for that lesson.
requirements.acceptance: Changing a student's default does not mutate historical lessons.

requirements.requirement: Lesson statuses are only SCHEDULED, COMPLETED, or CANCELLED; there is no makeup/보강 concept.
requirements.acceptance: No enum, field, filter, badge, or workflow named makeup/보강 exists.

requirements.requirement: Scheduled lessons support preparation notes and a lightweight preparation checklist.
requirements.acceptance: Prep text/checklist can be edited before class and is visible on Home and lesson detail.

requirements.requirement: Students support default fee amount and default lesson duration.
requirements.acceptance: New lessons prefill amount/duration and allow per-lesson overrides without changing history.

requirements.requirement: Recurring tutoring schedules capture weekday, start time, duration, timezone, and effective dates.
requirements.acceptance: Schedule generation is deterministic across Asia/Seoul daylight/time boundaries and avoids duplicates.

requirements.requirement: Online lessons can create a Google Calendar event and Google Meet conference.
requirements.acceptance: Authorized users can create/sync an event and open its Meet URL from the app.

requirements.requirement: Default Meet behavior generates unique conference data per lesson event; it must not copy conferenceData between unrelated events.
requirements.acceptance: Calendar adapter uses conferenceData.createRequest with conferenceDataVersion=1 for each generated lesson event.

requirements.requirement: A student may optionally store a manually supplied reusable Meet URL, clearly labeled as a user-managed exception.
requirements.acceptance: Manual fixed URL is never represented as copied Google conferenceData and can be disabled per lesson.

requirements.requirement: In-person students/lessons store a visit location and expose a location action instead of Meet.
requirements.acceptance: Lesson card displays the correct action for its mode.

requirements.requirement: Completing a lesson creates or updates exactly one receivable for the lesson amount.
requirements.acceptance: The operation is idempotent and covered by a transaction/integration test.

requirements.requirement: Lesson, receivable, and actual bank/financial transaction remain separate linked records.
requirements.acceptance: Unpaid completed work is representable without fake income, and paid income is traceable to its receivable.

requirements.requirement: Receivables support open, partially paid, paid, and void states plus allocations from one or more deposits.
requirements.acceptance: Partial and combined payments reconcile correctly and never exceed amount due.

requirements.requirement: Deposit matching suggests receivables using amount, payer/counterparty alias, student, and timing, but requires confirmation.
requirements.acceptance: Suggested matches show evidence and confidence; no match is committed without explicit approval.

requirements.requirement: Effective hourly income includes lesson time, preparation minutes, and travel minutes.
requirements.acceptance: Student and lesson analytics show nominal and effective hourly rates using documented formulas.

requirements.requirement: Student detail shows schedule, lesson history, monthly counts, earned amount, received amount, and outstanding receivables.
requirements.acceptance: All figures reconcile to ledger/receivable records for selected month.

requirements.requirement: Student records may store payer/deposit alias and operational notes, but no unnecessary sensitive school-record documents are uploaded in MVP.
requirements.acceptance: MVP contains no document upload flow; notes are access-controlled and minimal.

requirements.requirement: Money contains Overview, Accounts, Transactions, Receivables, Subscriptions, Grow, and Analytics.
requirements.acceptance: Every destination exists with coherent cross-links.

requirements.requirement: Accounts store institution, nickname, masked account number, type, currency, current balance, available balance, and last sync time.
requirements.acceptance: Account list/detail exposes those fields without displaying a full account number.

requirements.requirement: Account overview shows total included balance, per-account balance, monthly inflow, monthly outflow, and recent transactions.
requirements.acceptance: Totals exclude hidden/excluded accounts and transfers are not counted as income or expense.

requirements.requirement: Users can manually create income and expense records.
requirements.acceptance: Validated forms persist, edit, and delete manual ledger entries with audit timestamps.

requirements.requirement: Transaction kinds are INCOME, EXPENSE, or TRANSFER.
requirements.acceptance: Every ledger row has one kind and transfer rows use a linked transfer group.

requirements.requirement: Transfers between the user's accounts are excluded from income, expense, and spending analytics.
requirements.acceptance: Moving 100,000 KRW from bank to investment leaves net worth unchanged and adds zero spending.

requirements.requirement: Income categories include tutoring, scholarship, allowance, and other.
requirements.acceptance: Default categories are seeded and user categories can be managed in Settings.

requirements.requirement: Expense categories include food, cafe, transport, housing, shopping, education, subscription, household, and other.
requirements.acceptance: Default categories are seeded and categorization appears in analytics.

requirements.requirement: Transactions distinguish personal scope from household-linked scope.
requirements.acceptance: Household links point to shared expense/settlement records while personal transactions remain private.

requirements.requirement: Bank integrations are read-only in this product: account discovery/registration, balance inquiry, and transaction-history inquiry only.
requirements.acceptance: No withdrawal, deposit-transfer, payment initiation, or credential collection UI is implemented.

requirements.requirement: A BankProvider adapter supports MOCK, MANUAL_CSV, KFTC_TESTBED, and KFTC_PRODUCTION implementations.
requirements.acceptance: MVP runs fully with mock/manual providers; testbed/prod are isolated behind the same interface.

requirements.requirement: KFTC production mode remains disabled until institutional application, contract, eligibility, consent, and security requirements are satisfied.
requirements.acceptance: Feature flag and operator documentation prevent accidental production activation.

requirements.requirement: Manual CSV import is available as a fallback for transaction history before real bank onboarding.
requirements.acceptance: Importer provides preview, duplicate detection, mapping, and rollback-safe commit.

requirements.requirement: Imported bank transactions are idempotent using provider/external identifiers or a deterministic fingerprint.
requirements.acceptance: Re-sync/re-import creates no duplicates.

requirements.requirement: Transactions can be linked to receivables, subscription occurrences, shared expenses, settlements, and investment transfers without duplicate expense rows.
requirements.acceptance: Each linkage is traceable and uniqueness constraints prevent duplicate payment linkage.

requirements.requirement: The app distinguishes actual bank cash movement from economic responsibility in shared expenses.
requirements.acceptance: A user paying 100% of rent but owing 50% sees cash outflow 100% and personal burden 50%, with the remainder receivable from roommate.

requirements.requirement: Asset overview includes cash/account balances and tracked long-term investment value.
requirements.acceptance: Total assets and component values reconcile and transfers do not change total assets.

requirements.requirement: Account types may include bank, cash, card, investment, and other; card automation is not required in MVP.
requirements.acceptance: Schema supports all types while UI labels unsupported sync modes honestly.

requirements.requirement: Money analytics provide month selection and compare current month with a previous month.
requirements.acceptance: Comparison uses consistent date boundaries and indicates incomplete current-month data.

requirements.requirement: Earned but unpaid tutoring is shown separately from settled cash income and excluded from cash-based available surplus.
requirements.acceptance: Outstanding receivables never inflate account balance or settled-income totals.

requirements.requirement: Money contains a dedicated Subscriptions area for recurring paid services.
requirements.acceptance: Subscriptions is reachable from Money and dashboard cards link to filtered views.

requirements.requirement: Subscription dashboard shows normalized monthly total, projected annual total, upcoming renewals, trial endings, and unmatched/overdue occurrences.
requirements.acceptance: All metrics are derived from active records and occurrence/payment status.

requirements.requirement: Subscription statuses include trial, active, paused, cancelled, and ended.
requirements.acceptance: Status transitions preserve history and affect forecasts correctly.

requirements.requirement: Subscription categories include AI/software, cloud/storage, education, entertainment, communication, fitness, news, and other.
requirements.acceptance: Default categories exist and are filterable.

requirements.requirement: Subscription details store provider/name, plan, amount, currency, billing cycle, start date, and next charge date.
requirements.acceptance: Create/edit/detail flows expose and validate all fields.

requirements.requirement: Billing cycles support weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, yearly, and custom day interval.
requirements.acceptance: Monthly-equivalent formula tests cover every cycle including leap/year boundary cases.

requirements.requirement: Subscriptions support trial end, cancel-by date, auto-renew flag, and reminder-day offsets.
requirements.acceptance: Upcoming and trial-reminder queries use Asia/Seoul dates and avoid duplicate reminders.

requirements.requirement: Subscriptions can be personal or household scoped.
requirements.acceptance: Household subscriptions require a household and are visible to active household members without exposing private account data.

requirements.requirement: A household subscription stores payer and responsibility splits independently.
requirements.acceptance: 50:50, one-person-all, and custom split presets produce exact integer KRW allocations.

requirements.requirement: Subscriptions may reference a payment account/card, transaction descriptor pattern, service URL, notes, and last-used date.
requirements.acceptance: Optional fields are safe, editable, and not required for basic use.

requirements.requirement: Price history is retained when a subscription price changes.
requirements.acceptance: Editing amount creates an effective-dated history row and preserves past forecasts/payments.

requirements.requirement: Each expected charge is a SubscriptionOccurrence distinct from an actual financial transaction.
requirements.acceptance: Future dues exist before payment without creating fake bank spending.

requirements.requirement: Actual bank transactions can be matched to subscription occurrences using amount, descriptor, account, and date, with confirmation.
requirements.acceptance: Confirmed match marks occurrence paid and does not generate a duplicate expense.

requirements.requirement: A paid household subscription creates or links one shared expense and its splits rather than duplicate household/money records.
requirements.acceptance: One occurrence maps to at most one transaction and one shared expense.

requirements.requirement: Subscription calendar lists renewal dates and supports 7-day and 30-day filters.
requirements.acceptance: Calendar/list views agree across month boundaries.

requirements.requirement: Users can manually mark keep, review, or cancel-candidate decisions and record last-used date.
requirements.acceptance: The app never claims usage it cannot observe; decisions are explicitly user-entered.

requirements.requirement: Local-only insights may flag duplicate-category subscriptions or review candidates without recommending a specific commercial replacement.
requirements.acceptance: Insight explains its rule and source records; it is dismissible and deterministic.

requirements.requirement: Unpaid confirmed subscription obligations due in the planning window reduce actual available surplus, while already paid charges are not subtracted twice.
requirements.acceptance: Formula tests cover unpaid, matched, skipped, cancelled, and household split cases.

requirements.requirement: Cancellation/ending stops future occurrence generation but preserves historical occurrences and payments.
requirements.acceptance: History remains visible and forecasts exclude post-end dates.

requirements.requirement: Subscription reminders are represented in-app first; push/email delivery is optional future work.
requirements.acceptance: MVP has an in-app reminder center with no misleading unavailable notification toggle.

requirements.requirement: Grow implements one simple student-level method: monthly surplus allocation and recurring long-term contribution tracking.
requirements.acceptance: No stock picking, leverage, derivatives, auto-trading, or return guarantee appears.

requirements.requirement: Grow separates safety reserve, long-term contribution, and flexible money.
requirements.acceptance: Monthly plan and completion state show all three buckets.

requirements.requirement: Investment funding is modeled as an inter-account transfer, not an expense.
requirements.acceptance: Contribution transfer changes asset composition but not total assets or spending.

requirements.requirement: Grow tracks planned and completed monthly contribution amounts.
requirements.acceptance: A contribution can be pending, partially completed, completed, skipped, or cancelled.

requirements.requirement: Actual available surplus is the primary decision metric.
requirements.acceptance: Home and Grow display the same tested value for the selected planning period.

requirements.requirement: Actual available surplus starts from settled cash inflows, not billed or unpaid tutoring work.
requirements.acceptance: Open receivables are excluded until a linked payment transaction exists.

requirements.requirement: Actual available surplus subtracts personal expenses, the user's economic share of household costs, unpaid confirmed subscription/fixed obligations in the window, and required safety-reserve top-up, without double counting.
requirements.acceptance: Scenario tests document and verify every term.

requirements.requirement: The app displays actual cash remaining separately from responsibility-adjusted available surplus.
requirements.acceptance: Shared-expense prepayment/settlement scenarios show different but reconcilable figures.

requirements.requirement: Grow tracks current cash assets and long-term investment value for visibility only.
requirements.acceptance: Values are manual or account-derived and clearly timestamped.

requirements.requirement: Investment guidance is educational and neutral, discloses possible principal loss, and never promises performance.
requirements.acceptance: Copy review finds no guarantee, urgency, or personalized security recommendation.

requirements.requirement: A fixed monthly amount or percentage-of-available-surplus rule can define the contribution plan.
requirements.acceptance: Rules produce deterministic integer KRW planned amounts with a configurable cap.

requirements.requirement: Brokerage execution is explicitly out of scope; completed contributions are confirmed manually or matched to transfer transactions.
requirements.acceptance: There is no buy/sell endpoint or brokerage credential field.

requirements.requirement: Household is a separate shared data boundary from the user's private finance data.
requirements.acceptance: Roommate can access shared household records but never the user's private accounts/transactions.

requirements.requirement: Household supports owner/member roles and invite/active/left membership states.
requirements.acceptance: Invite acceptance and membership checks are enforced by RLS and tests.

requirements.requirement: Household overview shows shared monthly cost, user's share, roommate settlement balance, low-stock items, and cleaning status.
requirements.acceptance: Cards link to filtered detail and reconcile to source rows.

requirements.requirement: Inventory items store name, quantity, unit, ownership, storage location, optional expiry, low-stock threshold, and notes.
requirements.acceptance: Create/edit/detail flows and schema include every field.

requirements.requirement: Inventory ownership can be mine, roommate's, or shared, represented with member ownership rather than hard-coded labels.
requirements.acceptance: UI renders friendly labels for the current two-person household and schema supports additional members.

requirements.requirement: Inventory storage locations are refrigerated, frozen, or room temperature.
requirements.acceptance: List filters and validation use exactly those options in MVP.

requirements.requirement: Inventory quantity supports fast plus/minus adjustment with an audit-safe nonnegative result.
requirements.acceptance: Concurrent adjustment test prevents lost updates and negative quantity.

requirements.requirement: Low-stock items can create a shopping-list item.
requirements.acceptance: Action is idempotent and links shopping item to its inventory source.

requirements.requirement: Shopping items can be personal/member-owned or shared and can later link to a transaction/shared expense.
requirements.acceptance: Purchased status and linkage do not duplicate financial records.

requirements.requirement: Cleaning tasks store title, area, assignee, recurrence, last completion, next due time, and active state.
requirements.acceptance: Task creation and completion correctly advance the next due time.

requirements.requirement: Cleaning presents simple derived states: OK, due soon, and due/overdue.
requirements.acceptance: State is calculated from now, next due, and warning lead time rather than manually drifting.

requirements.requirement: Marking cleaning complete records who/when and recalculates schedule.
requirements.acceptance: Completion history is retained and next due is deterministic.

requirements.requirement: Shared expense categories include rent, management fee, electricity, gas, water, internet, household goods, shared groceries, subscription, and other.
requirements.acceptance: All categories are available and appear in monthly totals.

requirements.requirement: Shared expenses store actual payer separately from responsibility splits.
requirements.acceptance: Payer and split totals are independently editable before settlement.

requirements.requirement: Split presets support equal 50:50, user pays all, roommate pays all, and custom amounts/percentages.
requirements.acceptance: Rounding assigns every KRW exactly once and split sum equals total.

requirements.requirement: Household settlement computes the net amount one member owes the other across expenses and prior settlements.
requirements.acceptance: Pairwise netting test covers payer reversals, refunds, and partial settlements.

requirements.requirement: A bank deposit can be suggested and confirmed as a roommate settlement payment.
requirements.acceptance: Confirmed allocation changes settlement status and retains transaction traceability.

requirements.requirement: Household costs affect Money analytics and Grow using the user's responsibility share, with reconciliation to actual cash paid/received.
requirements.acceptance: No shared cost is omitted or counted twice in dashboard formulas.

requirements.requirement: A bank transaction can be classified as household shopping, housing, utility, or personal spending through a confirmation flow.
requirements.acceptance: Classification creates/links the correct shared expense only after confirmation.

requirements.requirement: Barcode scanning and receipt OCR are explicitly deferred; manual inventory/shopping flows must be fast enough for MVP.
requirements.acceptance: No fake OCR/barcode control exists in production UI.

requirements.requirement: Home shows today's lessons with student, tutoring type/subject, time, mode, preparation notes, and Meet/location action.
requirements.acceptance: Today's schedule is ordered and each lesson card has the correct primary action.

requirements.requirement: Home shows monthly tutoring forecast from active recurring schedules, earned, received, and outstanding amounts separately.
requirements.acceptance: Forecast is clearly labeled and reconciles to schedule/fee assumptions; earned, received, and outstanding match lesson/receivable/payment records; forecast is never treated as settled cash or available surplus.

requirements.requirement: Home shows total account balance, monthly settled income, and monthly expense.
requirements.acceptance: Transfers and unpaid receivables are excluded from income/expense.

requirements.requirement: Home shows subscriptions due soon and trial endings.
requirements.acceptance: Cards link to correctly filtered subscription views.

requirements.requirement: Home shows actual available surplus and current Grow plan status.
requirements.acceptance: Values match Grow page and formulas.

requirements.requirement: Home shows refrigerator low-stock alerts, cleaning due state, and roommate settlement balance.
requirements.acceptance: Each alert links to the source household module.

requirements.requirement: Home shows pending suggested matches for tutoring deposits, subscription charges, household expenses, and settlements.
requirements.acceptance: Suggestions can be reviewed, accepted, or dismissed without silent mutation.

requirements.requirement: Home prioritizes actions required today rather than presenting a dense finance dashboard.
requirements.acceptance: Mobile first viewport exposes today's actions before secondary analytics.

requirements.requirement: Google integration uses OAuth with the minimum Calendar scopes required for selected behavior.
requirements.acceptance: Consent screen/scopes are documented and tokens are server-only.

requirements.requirement: Calendar event creation stores external event ID, calendar link, Meet URL, sync state, and last sync error.
requirements.acceptance: Retry is idempotent using a stable app event identifier.

requirements.requirement: Calendar deletion/cancellation behavior is explicit and never silently deletes a user's unrelated event.
requirements.acceptance: Only events created or explicitly linked by the app can be mutated.

requirements.requirement: KFTC balance and transaction-history calls use server-side access tokens and fintech-use numbers, never browser storage.
requirements.acceptance: Threat model and implementation tests verify secrets are absent from client bundles/logs.

requirements.requirement: KFTC transaction pagination handles the provider page limit and incremental sync safely.
requirements.acceptance: Adapter follows next-page state and stops without duplicate or skipped records.

requirements.requirement: All external adapters have mock implementations and contract tests.
requirements.acceptance: The complete app can be demonstrated without real Google/KFTC credentials.

requirements.requirement: Sync jobs expose last success, last attempt, stale status, and actionable error messages.
requirements.acceptance: UI never presents stale balances as silently current.

requirements.requirement: External API retries are bounded and idempotent with structured logging and redaction.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cover timeout, rate limit, duplicate request, and provider error cases.

requirements.requirement: Vercel deployment and Supabase migrations use preview/development environments before production.
requirements.acceptance: Runbook requires preview verification and explicit production confirmation.

requirements.requirement: Google Calendar integration is an app API integration; a personal Google Calendar Codex plugin is optional for developer workflow and is not an application dependency.
requirements.acceptance: Application runs without any Codex connector installed.

requirements.requirement: Korean is the only required UI language in MVP, with plain student-friendly copy.
requirements.acceptance: No mixed-language production labels except unavoidable service names.

requirements.requirement: Desktop uses a sidebar and mobile uses bottom navigation with a clear global add action.
requirements.acceptance: Navigation remains reachable, keyboard accessible, and safe-area aware.

requirements.requirement: Forms use progressive disclosure and conditional fields instead of enterprise-style dense screens.
requirements.acceptance: Student, subscription, and shared-expense forms reveal only relevant fields.

requirements.requirement: All destructive and cross-record linking actions require confirmation and explain effects.
requirements.acceptance: Delete, cancel, match, settle, unlink, and regenerate actions have safe dialogs/undo where practical.

requirements.requirement: Accessibility targets WCAG 2.2 AA for color contrast, focus, labels, semantics, and touch targets.
requirements.acceptance: Automated accessibility checks pass and manual keyboard/screen-reader smoke checks are documented.

requirements.requirement: Dates and money are formatted consistently with clear month filters and no timezone ambiguity.
requirements.acceptance: All date formatting routes through shared utilities and tests.

requirements.requirement: Charts are secondary to readable numbers and lists and have accessible text equivalents.
requirements.acceptance: Every chart has a table/summary and works without color alone.

requirements.requirement: PWA supports basic offline shell and read-only cached recent data, while writes require network and show pending state only if safely queued.
requirements.acceptance: Offline behavior is honest and never pretends a financial write succeeded.

requirements.requirement: No placeholder button may ship without either a working action or an explicit disabled/deferred explanation.
requirements.acceptance: E2E crawl finds no dead interactive controls.

requirements.requirement: Every page has empty-state guidance based on the user's next useful action.
requirements.acceptance: New-account demo can reach a useful first record from each empty page.

requirements.requirement: Supabase Row Level Security is enabled on every user or household data table.
requirements.acceptance: Automated RLS tests prove cross-user and nonmember access is denied.

requirements.requirement: Private finance rows are owner-only; household rows are available only to active household members.
requirements.acceptance: Roommate cannot query accounts, private transactions, bank connections, or private subscriptions.

requirements.requirement: OAuth/bank refresh tokens and secrets are never stored in plaintext application tables or client-accessible environment variables.
requirements.acceptance: Secrets use a server-side encrypted secret reference and are redacted from logs/errors.

requirements.requirement: Service-role keys, provider secrets, and PATs are excluded from version control and browser bundles.
requirements.acceptance: Secret scanning and bundle checks pass; .env files are ignored.

requirements.requirement: External access follows least privilege and explicit consent, with disconnect/revoke controls.
requirements.acceptance: Integrations page shows scopes/status and supports safe disconnect.

requirements.requirement: Sensitive student, household, and financial values are minimized in logs and analytics.
requirements.acceptance: Structured logger redacts names, account identifiers, notes, and tokens by default.

requirements.requirement: Input validation, output encoding, CSRF/session protection, rate limits, and authorization checks apply to server mutations.
requirements.acceptance: Security tests and review cover OWASP-relevant paths.

requirements.requirement: Data export and account deletion are available with explicit confirmation and retention behavior.
requirements.acceptance: User can export owned/shared-relevant data and request deletion without orphaning required settlement history incorrectly.

requirements.requirement: The app documents that finance figures are informational and may be stale; it is not a bank, broker, tax adviser, or investment adviser.
requirements.acceptance: Relevant screens and terms include concise disclaimers without obstructing normal use.

requirements.requirement: Development MCP tools are scoped to development/test projects and never connected to production financial or personal data by default.
requirements.acceptance: MCP setup file defaults Supabase to project-scoped read-only and marks production prohibited.

requirements.requirement: Dependency, migration, and security scans run in CI before merge/deploy.
requirements.acceptance: CI includes typecheck, lint, tests, build, migration checks, secret scan, and dependency/security review.

requirements.requirement: Every match/reconciliation decision retains an audit record of actor, timestamp, source, and prior/new linkage.
requirements.acceptance: Audit history can explain why each receivable, subscription, shared expense, or settlement was marked paid.

requirements.requirement: Receipt OCR is a future enhancement, not MVP.
requirements.acceptance: Tracked in backlog only.

requirements.requirement: Barcode scanning is a future enhancement, not MVP.
requirements.acceptance: Tracked in backlog only.

requirements.requirement: AI-assisted transaction categorization and monthly reports are future enhancements and require explainability/confirmation.
requirements.acceptance: Tracked in backlog only; no fake AI in MVP.

requirements.requirement: Broader budgets, fixed recurring income/expense rules, cards, and richer asset allocation are future enhancements.
requirements.acceptance: Tracked in backlog only.

requirements.requirement: Push/email reminder delivery is future work after in-app reminders.
requirements.acceptance: Tracked in backlog only.

requirements.requirement: No brokerage auto-execution or open-banking transfer initiation is planned for MVP.
requirements.acceptance: Tracked as explicitly excluded unless separately redesigned and approved.
